tools.name: get_quote_request_checklist
tools.description: The information People Can Build needs to quote an exhibition stand (show, city, dates, sqm, stand type, design status, scope, budget range, special items, confidentiality). tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Send a real quote request to People Can Build (creates an enquiry read by a person; reply by email usually within one business day). ALWAYS confirm the details with the user before calling. Required: name, email, message. Do not promise prices beyond the public ranges.

tools.name: get_quote_status
tools.description: Status of a quote request previously submitted via request_quote. Needs the ticket id (PCB-XXXXXX) AND the e-mail address used on the request; returns the current status, any note from the project manager and the status history. Does not return the request contents.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_quote_request_checklist" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_field_notes, get_quote_request_checklist, request_quote, get_quote_status · Private data: get_company_profile · Public sink: estimate_design_fee, get_quote_request_checklist, request_quote.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_field_notes, get_quote_request_checklist, request_quote, get_quote_status · Private data: get_company_profile · Public sink: estimate_design_fee, get_quote_request_checklist, request_quote

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
